I need to determine the molecular formula of a molecule in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry using ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique. 

Mass spectrometry will give me mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios of ions, which can help me determine the molecular weight of the compound. From the molecular weight and the mass spectrum pattern, I can deduce the molecular formula.

Let me start by obtaining the mass spectrometry data.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak at m/z 262.09937969036 (100% intensity)
- Isotope peaks at m/z 263.10, 264.11, 265.11, etc. with decreasing intensities

The base peak at m/z 262.099 likely represents [M+H]+ or [M-H]- depending on the ionization mode. In ESI, positive mode typically gives [M+H]+ ions.

If this is [M+H]+, then the molecular weight would be approximately 261.099.

Looking at the isotope pattern:
- M+1 peak is about 19.7% of base peak
- M+2 peak is about 2.25% of base peak

The M+1 peak intensity of ~19.7% suggests the presence of carbon atoms (each carbon contributes ~1.1% due to 13C). This would indicate approximately 19.7/1.1 ≈ 18 carbon atoms.

The M+2 peak of ~2.25% could come from:
1. Two 13C atoms: C(C-1)/2 × 1.1² ≈ 18×17/2 × 0.0121 ≈ 1.85%
2. Additional contribution from other elements

For a molecular weight of ~261 with ~18 carbons (216 mass units), we have ~45 mass units remaining for H, O, N, and other elements.

Let me consider common molecular formulas around this mass:
- C18H15NO (MW = 261.115)
- C15H15NO3 (MW = 257.105)
- C14H15NO4 (MW = 261.100)

C14H15NO4 has MW = 14×12 + 15×1 + 14 + 4×16 = 168 + 15 + 14 + 64 = 261.100

This matches very closely with 261.099!

Let me verify: C14H15NO4
- Exact mass: 14×12.000 + 15×1.008 + 14.003 + 4×15.999 = 168.000 + 15.120 + 14.003 + 63.996 = 261.119

Actually, let me recalculate more precisely:
C14H15NO4 exact mass = 14×12.0000 + 15×1.00783 + 1×14.00307 + 4×15.99491 = 168.0000 + 15.11745 + 14.00307 + 63.97964 = 261.10016

This is very close to 262.099 - 1.008 = 261.091 (if we assume [M+H]+)

The molecular formula is likely C14H15NO4.
</thought>
